name: Bayrock Group

summary.text: Bayrock Group LLC is a New York real-estate firm associated with Tevfik Arif and Felix Sater. It co-developed Trump SoHo, a 46-story condominium hotel at 246 Spring Street in Manhattan, with the Sapir Organization and a Trump Organization affiliate; Donald Trump licensed his name and received an 18 percent equity stake without investing capital. In 2007 the Icelandic investment company FL Group invested $50 million in Bayrock projects including Trump SoHo. In 2010 former Bayrock finance director Jody Kriss sued Bayrock, Arif and Sater under the RICO statute alleging money laundering and tax evasion, allegations the defendants denied; the case was settled in principle in February 2018 on undisclosed terms.

facts.claim: Trump SoHo, a 46-story condominium hotel at 246 Spring Street, was a joint venture of Bayrock Group, the Sapir Organization and a Trump Organization affiliate; Trump said in a deposition that he received an 18 percent equity share of the building in exchange for licensing his name, and reporting states he invested no capital in construction.
facts.quote: in a legal deposition, Trump said he also got an 18 percent equity share of the building

facts.claim: In 2007 FL Group, an Icelandic investment company, invested $50 million in several Bayrock projects linked to Trump, including a development in Whitestone, Queens and Trump SoHo in Manhattan; FL Group was dissolved in 2014.
facts.quote: In 2007, the FL Group invested $50 million in several Bayrock projects linked to Trump, including a development in Whitestone, Queens, and Trump SoHo in Manhattan.

facts.claim: The Daily Telegraph reported in May 2016 that Trump signed approval documents for the FL Group deal and that the equity investment was later recast as a loan; Trump's attorney Alan Garten said Trump 'had nothing to do with the transaction', that his signature was a formality and that he was only a limited partner.
facts.quote: Trump's attorney, Alan Garten, responded that Trump "had nothing to do with the transaction," with his signature merely a formality and Trump only a "limited partner" in the property.

sources.title: Trump signed off on $50M Trump SoHo investment that turned into loan: report

facts.claim: In 2010 Jody Kriss, a former Bayrock finance director, sued Bayrock and its principals alleging that the firm laundered money, evaded taxes and cheated him out of millions; Bayrock and Sater rejected the allegations, with their lawyers describing Kriss as a disgruntled former employee. These were allegations, not findings.
facts.quote: He alleged that Felix Sater and Tevfik Arif's real estate firm laundered money, evaded taxes and bilked him out of millions.

sources.title: Trump-Linked Real Estate Firm Settles Suit by Ex-Employee
Kriss, Bayrock agree to settle lawsuit after 8 years

facts.claim: Kriss's complaint alleged that FL Group bought 62 percent of the profits from four Bayrock properties including Trump SoHo and that the deal was structured as a loan to avoid taxes; a 2010 filing cited a confidential informant who said money came from Arif's brother in Russia with access to cash accounts at a chromium refinery in Kazakhstan. These allegations were not adjudicated.
facts.quote: According to Kriss's complaint, FL Group bought 62 percent of the profits from four Bayrock properties, which was the developer's entire stake.

sources.title: Why Did a Russia-Friendly Icelandic Fund Want To Invest In Trump Projects?

facts.claim: On December 2, 2016 Judge Lorna G. Schofield of the Southern District of New York issued an opinion in Kriss v. Bayrock Group LLC, No. 10 Civ. 3959, in which plaintiffs Jody Kriss and Michael Chu'di Ejekam sued under RICO and state law, alleging the Arif/Sater agreement created a RICO enterprise operated as Bayrock Group; the case had been sealed until 2016.
facts.quote: The amended complaint alleges that the Arif/Satter agreement set up a RICO enterprise, operated in the form of Bayrock Group (the "Bayrock Group Enterprise" or "Enterprise").

facts.quote: The Bayrock Group, the developer of the Trump Soho building in Manhattan, agreed in principle to settle a lawsuit filed in 2010 by former finance director Jody Kriss.

openQuestions: The December 2016 opinion's holding on which RICO claims proceeded was not visible in the excerpts reached; read the full opinion on CourtListener or Leagle.
Trump SoHo construction start (2006) and opening date (2008 vs 2010) differ between sources; only reference sites were reached for the 2006 groundbreaking.
The Kazakh chromium-refinery allegation rests on a 2010 court filing citing a confidential informant; it has not been adjudicated.
